# Environment Variables

How a value gets from the host into a sandbox process, and which layer owns
which value.

## The rule

**`/sandbox/.env` has exactly two sources.**

1. **The operator's `OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_<NAME>` exports** on the host that runs
   `sandbox.sh --create` or `--refresh`. Each one is written as `<NAME>`.
2. **The OTEL identity block** below — dynamic per-sandbox values that cannot
   be written by hand.

Nothing else is patched in. No host variable is captured by name any more:
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, the Jira tokens, bound-provider keys and every tool
setting arrive only when the operator exports the prefixed form for that
create/refresh. Setting those variables is the operator's responsibility.

A sandbox's profile still decides the network policy and which credential files
are uploaded. It no longer decides which env vars travel: the prefix does, on
every profile. `validate-profile.sh` checks for the variables it needs *inside*
the sandbox — that is past the injection boundary and is allowed.

`tests/test-sandbox-env.sh` proves the prefix rule, that only exported names
travel, that an unexported shell variable does not, that a non-prefixed name
never ships, and that the OTEL identity block survives.

## Variables to set

Export the prefixed form. The table names the value the sandbox sees.

### Claude Code credentials

| Sandbox variable | When | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | personal/home signing in with an API key (not OAuth); work when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is set | Claude Code authentication. With a provider URL this is the provider's key. |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | work, when Claude runs against a bound non-Anthropic provider | Selects the provider. The work policy reaches it through the provider binding; `validate-profile.sh` probes it. **API root only, no `/v1`**: Claude Code appends `/v1/messages`, so `https://host/v1` becomes `https://host/v1/v1/messages` and the connection is reset. `validate-profile.sh` cannot catch it — its GET on the base URL is not a 403, so it reports reachable. |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY` | with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | A provider model id is not in the CLI's own catalog. |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` | `0` with a provider URL; `1` for Vertex | Claude Code treats the variable's **presence** as "use Vertex". Unset with a provider URL makes the TUI ignore that URL and dial the blocked `api.anthropic.com`. |
| `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID` | Vertex path | Project the Vertex requests bill to. |
| `CLOUD_ML_REGION` | Vertex path | Vertex region. |
| `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` | Vertex path | Default project for Google client libraries. |
| `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | Vertex path, as `/sandbox/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json` | The host's path does not exist in the container; the file itself is uploaded by the create path. |
| `CLOUDSDK_CONFIG` | Vertex path, as `/sandbox/.config/gcloud` | Same reason. |

### Claude Code runtime knobs

`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TURNS`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS`,
`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` — export
them prefixed only if the sandbox should run with that value.
`tests/test-sandbox-env.sh` covers the pass-through shape.

### Jira

| Sandbox variable | Why |
|---|---|
| `JIRA_TOKEN`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN` | Jira API authentication. Tools disagree on the name; export whichever the tooling in the sandbox reads. |
| `JIRA_USERNAME`, `JIRA_EMAIL` | Account identity for Jira lookups. |
| `JIRA_URL` | Jira base URL. `validate-profile.sh` checks for it. |
| `JIRA_CLOUD_ID` | Jira Cloud id, for tools that need the cloud-scoped API. |

The host-side context generators (`scripts/lib.sh`, `scode`) read the plain
names from the host shell; they are separate from what the sandbox receives.

### Bound Codex/OpenCode providers

A bound provider config names env vars in `env_key` and `env_http_headers`.
The names for a sandbox are recorded in
`~/sandboxes/<name>/provider-profile-bindings.json` under `.keys`; export each
one prefixed, e.g. `OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_OPENAI_API_KEY`.
`tests/test-provider-profile-config.sh` covers the binding side.

### Dashboard and review tooling

| Sandbox variable | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_DASHBOARD_HOST` | `host.containers.internal` | The uploaded dashboard hooks relay to host tooling through the container gateway. |
| `REVIEW_ORCHESTRATOR_HARNESS` | `claude` | `jewzaam-reviews` orchestrator backend. |
| `REVIEW_ORCHESTRATOR_MODEL_DEEP` | e.g. `sonnet` | Model for deep review stages. |
| `REVIEW_ORCHESTRATOR_MODEL_FOCUSED` | e.g. `haiku` | Model for focused review stages. |

## The OTEL exception

Telemetry identity and its query endpoints are written automatically. They are
dynamic — the collector address comes from `config/site.env`, the rest from the
sandbox's own identity — and nobody can type them by hand.

| Sandbox variable | Source | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | `OTEL_URL` in `config/site.env` | Claude Code / Codex exporters |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` | fixed `http/protobuf` | exporters (the proxy is HTTP/1.1 only; gotcha 13) |
| `SANDBOX_PROMETHEUS_URL` | `PROMETHEUS_URL` in `config/site.env` | `validate-profile.sh` |
| `SANDBOX_LOKI_URL` | `LOKI_URL` in `config/site.env` | `validate-profile.sh` |
| `SANDBOX_PROVIDER_URLS` | bound provider resolution | `validate-profile.sh` |
| `SANDBOX_SOURCE_NAME` | sandbox name | OTEL enrichment |
| `SANDBOX_HOST_NAME` | creating host's `hostname` | OTEL `host.name` |
| `SANDBOX_HOST_DIR` | `~/sandboxes/<name>` | OTEL `project` |
| `SANDBOX_OPENSHELL_NAME` | `manifest.json` `.openshell_name` | ties a session to its container |
| `SANDBOX_PROFILE` | profile | `harness-wrapper.sh` model choice, `validate-profile.sh` |
| `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` | assembled from the rows above | every telemetry consumer; downstream code appends to it |

The prefixed exports are written **last**, so
`OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` (or any of the rows above)
overrides the computed value.

Container telemetry policy — which exporters, intervals, log detail — stays in
`config/bashrc`, baked into the image. It is not patched in per sandbox and can
be overridden the same prefixed way.

## Harness configs cannot inject env

Any agentic harness config that could patch env vars in has them stripped:

- **Claude Code `settings.json`** — the entire `env` block is removed, on every
  profile (`scripts/strip-settings.py`; `tests/test-strip-settings.sh`).
- **OpenCode `opencode.json`** — top-level `env`, and inline provider keys
  (`providers[].settings.apiKey` / `api_key`), are removed
  (`stage_opencode_config`; `tests/test-opencode-config.sh`). `providers[].env`
  stays: it names the env var a provider reads, it does not set one.
- **Codex `config.toml`** — generated from an allowlist of top-level keys and
  tables, so host `shell_environment_policy` and MCP server `env` tables never
  travel (`render_codex_config`; `tests/test-render-codex-config.sh`).

A host that relied on one of those blocks exports the prefixed variable
instead.

## Create, refresh, and removal

`.env` is regenerated from the exports of the current run and re-uploaded on
every create and `--refresh`. `--refresh` deletes the sandbox's `.env` first,
so a variable the operator stopped exporting is gone afterwards — it is not
merged into the previous file.

## Example

```bash
export OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_JIRA_TOKEN=...
export OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_JIRA_URL=https://example.atlassian.net
export OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_OPENAI_API_KEY=...
scripts/sandbox.sh --create review-123 --profile work
unset OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_JIRA_TOKEN OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_JIRA_URL \
      OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_OPENAI_API_KEY
```

The sandbox then sees `JIRA_TOKEN`, `JIRA_URL`, and `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

## What still arrives as files

Env was one path, never the only one. Credential files are uploaded by the
create path: Claude OAuth (`.claude/.credentials.json`), Codex
(`.codex/auth.json`, work only), gcloud, gws, and the host `settings.json`
(minus its env block and host paths). Those are file copies, not env vars, and
are documented in the project `CLAUDE.md`.
